title: Separate code-guessing risk from session controls.
comment:
**Separate code-guessing risk from session controls.**

Student codes use the predictable `BP-${24000 + seq}` format. A single Redis session and a short token TTL do not prevent code guessing. A guessed code with `replaceSession: true` can replace the current session. Record this revocation risk and consider non-sequential codes, a replace cooldown, and student notification.

- Student Unique ID login is single-factor by product choice; mitigated by one active Redis session (`sid` in JWT), confirm-to-replace on conflict, auth rate limits, and short access-token TTL.
+ Student Unique ID login is single-factor by product choice. Student codes use the predictable `BP-${24000 + seq}` format. One active Redis session (`sid` in JWT) and a short access-token TTL do not prevent code guessing. A guessed code with `replaceSession: true` can replace the current session and revoke the real student's access during an exam. The auth rate limit slows guessing but does not prevent distributed attempts. Consider non-sequential codes, a replace cooldown, and student notification on replacement.
